findings.title: Ultimates and third abilities lose the fighter's signature in play: 18/32 a3/ult slots read as team orange or as shared white/glass neutrals
findings.what:
Confirmed and refined.

The a1/a2 colour gate passes on every slot, but a3 and ult were never gated. In play, 18 of 32 a3/ult slots fail the same >= 0.5 signature-share metric, 9 of them ultimates. A 19th, Kemdo a3, is a false pass.

Two causes:
- **Team light dominates** (Dunsom a3/ult, Hesmi a3, Burdam a3/ult, Nurrow ult, Rishal a3, Ervet ult, Kemdo a3). A few team-keyed layers (an emissive-10 shockwave ring, the Long Glint decals, Hesmi a3's pillar) carry 36-95 % of the light the VFX add.
- **Fixed neutrals carry the effect** (Tunlan a3/ult, Ilsheta a3/ult, Hesmi ult, Vashil a3/ult, Ervet a3, Rishal ult, Ardit a3). Warm white/cream (#F3E3C2, #F7EBD0), Dawnglass #BFD3E6 or ice #B6CEE0 do the work, and the signature-keyed layers (often gradient tails such as "#BFD3E6" → "signature") add about 0 % of the light.

The content layer counts meet r12's M12 spec on every slot (team 0-22 % of emissive layers, signature mostly >= 50 %). The defect is the share of light in play, not authoring counts.

Reviewer wording corrected:
- Tunlan's ult is not 'orange rims'. The orange in that shot is the enemy cone telegraph, a legitimate indicator; the effect itself is about 10 % team light and about 48 % white/cream.
- Ilsheta's help effects are mainly warm white (0.49-0.57 white), with team at 16-21 % of the light.

findings.title: Dynamic resolution stays blind when the GPU is the bottleneck on Chrome/Metal, and Ultra misses 60 fps on the reference M5
findings.what:
On ANGLE Metal the EXT_disjoint_timer_query reading is far longer than the frame interval, even at a steady 60 fps.
- quality.ts:159 drops every reading longer than the frame interval.
- When a window had readings but none were kept, quality.ts:166 classes it as not GPU-bound, so `late && gpuBound` never fires.
- The scale therefore never steps down when the GPU is the bottleneck: the one case the controller exists for.

Ultra at 1080p is GPU-bound on the M5 (renderer CPU 1.3-3.3 ms) and runs 33-51 fps, with frames alternating 33 and 16 ms.

Every new profile starts at High (src/session/settings.ts:65). No hardware detection exists (grep finds no deviceMemory, hardwareConcurrency or WEBGL_debug_renderer_info in src).

Result: a Mac Chrome player whose GPU cannot carry the default High preset at their resolution gets no automatic help.
findings.evidence:
Verifier's direct test: `node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4968ca64-9c2e-4f26-ac80-9c1269c9a02e/scratchpad/verify/verify_dyn.mjs --sec 20` (production bench _harness/_prod/dist, RIFT t 900 seed 7, densest fight) wraps the live renderer's DynamicResolution.sample and logs every (interval, cpu, gpu) it is fed. Report: _harness/_reports/closing_perf_verify_dyn.json and .log (load 2.8-3.3).
- High 1080p, dynamic resolution on: 60.0 fps, 0 of 1201 frames dropped. GPU readings p5 / p50 / p95 = 14.8 / 29.7 / 33.6 ms; 90.8 % are longer than the frame they were fed with.
- Ultra 1080p, dynamic resolution on: 33.1 fps, 526 of 662 frames dropped. 100 % of the readings are over the interval (p50 114.5 ms), 0 kept. Renderer CPU 1.32 ms. All 19 one-second windows read scale 1 and bound 'cpu'; 0 scale changes.
- High 3840x2160 (a GPU-bound stand-in for a weaker GPU at the default preset): 16.8 fps with dynamic resolution off, 13.5 fps with it on. 100 % of the readings are over the interval (p50 270 ms). Scale 1 in every window, bound 'cpu', CPU 1.58 ms.
- Shots: _harness/_shots/closing_perf_verify_dyn_ultra_1920x1080_dyn1.png (HUD reads 'ultra 35 fps 1.3 ms cpu, scale 1') and closing_perf_verify_dyn_high_3840x2160_dyn1.png.

Gate (closing_perf_verify_gate.json): Ultra 45.1 and 43.6 fps, 150 / 166 frames dropped, p95 33.4 ms, renderer CPU 2.3-3.3 ms. The reviewer read 51.4 fps and the integration gate 40.7.

The gate's own dynres step at High, during a load spike (3.22 to 6.22), fell to 44-52 fps for about 25 s. GPU readings were 44-89 ms, the window was labelled 'cpu', and the scale held at 1.0.

Code: src/render/quality.ts:155-170 (drop rule at :159, gpuBound at :166) and the header at :22-24, which explains the drop rule as a contention guard. src/render/renderer.ts:1005-1018.
findings.fix:
1. Treat the GPU timer as untrusted for the session when, in on-target windows, most readings exceed the frame interval. With an untrusted timer, fall back to the CPU rule: a late window with renderer + pump CPU < 60 % of the target is GPU-bound. Step down 0.05.
2. Add a perf_1080 --prod step that forces a GPU-bound frame (Ultra at 1080p, or High at 2x render scale) with dynamic resolution on. Assert the scale leaves base within 10 s and fps recovers to 58 or more.
3. First-run calibration: 3 s at High on the Home vale. If p95 > 18 ms, start at Medium or Low, with a VALE-styled notice linking Settings.
4. Rebalance Ultra (full AO, 4096 shadows) until it holds 60 on the reference machine, or gate it.
findings.files: src/render/quality.ts:150-170; src/render/renderer.ts:1000-1035; src/session/settings.ts:65; src/ui/screens/settings.tsx; _harness/perf_1080.mjs (dynres step)
findings.gauge:
League of Legends targets 60 fps at 1080p on mid hardware (r12 B4). Riot ties its graphics settings to hardware tiers: the minimum Mac spec (M1, 8 GB unified memory) is paired with Low settings, the recommended spec with High (Riot support, minimum and recommended system requirements). LoL has no dynamic resolution, so the gauge is the result, not the mechanism: the default and top presets must hold 60 on the machines they are offered on.

VALE offers Ultra on the reference M5 and it misses 60. It defaults every machine to High. And its one fps safety net cannot engage on Chrome/Metal.
findings.split: Controller, Ultra rebalance and the calibration API are CW1; the default preset in src/session/settings.ts and the VALE-styled notice in settings.tsx are CW3.

findings.title: A play session climbs to about 4.7 GB across Chrome's renderer and GPU processes and gives none of it back
findings.what:
The audio buffer map (src/audio/index.ts:328) and the GLB model map (src/render/assets.ts:34) have no budget and no eviction. grep finds no buffers.delete or models.delete.
- Every decoded music bed and cue stays as 48 kHz stereo float.
- Every model's images stay decoded, with an uncompressed GPU copy. No KTX2 or Basis path exists in src/render or tools/build_content.ts.

Memory steps up with each new map and only plateaus once the content runs out. After one pass over the three maps it sits at about 4.7 GB. Identical rebuilds are flat (PERF-M1 is closed), so this is unbudgeted cache, not a per-match leak.

Verifier, extended to all maps: `node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4968ca64-9c2e-4f26-ac80-9c1269c9a02e/scratchpad/verify/verify_mem.mjs --dev /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4968ca64-9c2e-4f26-ac80-9c1269c9a02e/scratchpad/closing_perf/devb --maps rift,bridge,fray,rift` gives _harness/_reports/closing_perf_verify_mem.json and .log. Samples are taken at Home after a forced GC; process footprints come from macOS `footprint`.

| At Home after | 0 matches | RIFT | +BRIDGE | +FRAY | +RIFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Renderer process (MB) | 124 | 1491 | 2099 | 2405 | 2438 |
| GPU process (MB) | 787 | 1536 | 1954 | 2237 | 2263 |
| Decoded audio (MB, buffers) | 0 | 361 (348) | 524 (497) | 657 (529) | 658 (530) |
| Models / texture pixels (MB, RGBA) | 0 / 0 | 79 / 602 | 102 / 891 | 117 / 1029 | 117 / 1029 |

- Six 58.6 MB match beds stay resident: mus_match_rift, mus_match_bridge and mus_match_fray, each with its _intense version.
- JS heap is only 53-83 MB; the cost lives outside the heap.
- Renderer plus GPU: 4.64 GB after three maps, 4.70 GB after the fourth match (+1.3 %).

Matches the reviewer's RIFT-only run: 2282 + 2313 MB after 4 matches (closing_perf_memsplit.json). Control: gate memory step +1.7 % (closing_perf_verify_gate.json).
findings.fix:
1. Ship model textures as KTX2 (UASTC for normal and ORM maps, ETC1S for albedo) and load them with KTX2Loader.
2. Close each ImageBitmap after upload, and re-fetch on context restore (keep probe_ctxloss passing).
3. Keep only the playing music bed decoded and free the previous one on a bed change, or stream beds through a media element. Keep cue buffers only for the current match's fighters plus the UI set.
4. Give the model and cue caches a byte budget with eviction at match end; keep the Home showcase and the next match's set.
5. Add a perf_1080 --prod step: RIFT, BRIDGE, FRAY, RIFT in one page. Assert renderer + GPU footprint at Home stays at or under 2.5 GB.

findings.gauge: LoL starts each game in a fresh game process, so memory returns to baseline after every match, and it ships its textures compressed for the GPU. Riot's minimum Mac spec is an M1 with 8 GB of unified memory (Riot support, minimum and recommended system requirements). On that machine VALE's two browser processes alone would hold about 4.7 GB of the 8 GB, which the GPU shares, after one pass over the three maps.
findings.split: KTX2 textures, model cache budget and the footprint gate are CW1; decoded-audio budget and bed eviction in src/audio/index.ts are CW2.

- Shots: _harness/_shots/closing_hesmi_portrait_face_x3.png, closing_hesmi_icon_48px_x4.png, closing_hesmi_icon_26px_x8.png, closing_hesmi_eye_a1_lunge_x3.png, closing_hesmi_portraits_3up.png (all three skins); art/out/fighters/hesmi/icon.png at 128 px has the strongest teeth read.

polish.title: Objective contests are thin: Sunsplinter waits about 9 min, Longshade is taken late and only to close
polish.what:
The numbers are real, but the major framing does not hold up:
- **Longshade as the closer** is a recorded design decision (modes_economy.md:358, owner ruling 4: 'the signed-off numbers stay ... it is the game's closer'). It is mostly a selection effect: with the buff emptied, the taker still wins 36/50.
- **The Sunsplinter delay** comes from the same lane-phase gate as CL-1 (bot.ts:432-439: during laning an objective is taken only from the adjacent lane on an opening, and the jungler too waits for an opening). CL-1's fix addresses it, so a separate major double-counts it.
- **What remains** is the defenders' answer to an empowered Longshade wave, a follow-up named in §9 and not done, and Splinters, which the design says stacks to 3 (modes_economy.md:399) but which the sim and content only refresh (content/team_buffs.json $comment). That leaves Sunsplinter weak.
polish.files: src/sim/bots/bot.ts (:432-439), src/sim/bots/team.ts (objective intent, defend), src/sim/core.ts (addTeamBuff stacking), content/team_buffs.json, _harness/probe_sim_bot_soak.ts
polish.gauge: LoL contests its early dragon-type objectives within a few minutes of spawn. The late boss is a strong but not certain closer; the reviewer's 80–88 % first-Baron figure is unverified. VALE's design accepts Longshade as a closer, which is not a gap by itself. The gaps are the uncontested first Sunsplinter, which is CL-1's root cause, and defenders who never answer an empowered wave.

polish.title: The lane hold can leave a base undefended: Hourbell lost at 13.2 min with 6 takedowns

Result: core at 13.2 min, 6 takedowns, team 0 loses 12 structures between 7.4 and 13.2 min (closing_gameplay_verify_vet8.json).

Across 40 games, 7 have a structure fall before the first takedown, and 3 lose a Lantern before 14:00.

|---|---|---|---|

polish.title: Tier separation misses the 85 % bar on seed windows the tuning has not seen

polish.title: Per-fighter RIFT balance can't be measured: harness lineups lock teammates together
polish.what: pacing.ts and probe_sim_bot_soak.ts seat each role as natives[role][(seed + slot + team) % n]. With 3 natives in most roles, the same fighters always share a team, so their win rates are confounded.

polish.title: Personal highlight banners put 'You' into a third-person line ('You takes five in a row.'), and the banner queue has no priority
polish.what:
Every personal first takedown, multikill, streak and shutdown sub-line conjugates for a third person while the name is 'You'.
The announcer queue is FIFO with no priority: it holds at most 2 pending and drops the oldest. A 5-kill ace therefore shows the team-wipe banner first, the streak second, and the 'Full peal' headline last, 7.1 s after the kills.
polish.evidence:
Reviewer: closing_hud_E02_takedown_banner.png ('You opens the count.').
Mine (closing_hud_verify_capture.json steps.ace, five enemies taken down in one tick by you), the banner sequence:
- at 8 ms: 'Lamps out | The other team is all down. Press the advantage.'
- at 3640 ms: 'Blazing | You has 5 takedowns without falling.'
- at 7137 ms: 'Full peal | You takes five in a row. Every bell is ringing.'
Shots: _harness/_shots/closing_hud_verify_03_banner_0..2.png.
Code:
- strings at content/strings.en.json:773 and :781-799;
- 'You' comes from model.ts:338 nameOf -> killfeed.you;
- the FIFO queue is model.ts:306-311 (`bannerQ.push`; `if (bannerQ.length > 2) bannerQ.shift()`).
polish.fix:
1. Add `.you.sub` second-person variants and pick them when the actor is you, as the reviewer suggests.
2. Give Banner a priority (multikill 5 > 4 > team wipe > shutdown > streak > first takedown > takedown).
3. Let a higher priority pre-empt the queue and collapse lower kill banners from the same tick. Keep the 3.5 s hold.
4. Add a strings lint for '{name} <verb>s' lines.
polish.gauge: LoL's personal announcements are written for the scorer, and a multikill takes precedence over the ace call, so the biggest moment is never last or ungrammatical.

polish.title: Death recap: damage-type chips can overflow, and the recap has no crowd-control time
polish.what:

closing_hud_F02_recap.png (and _full) show 'Physical 171' and 'Piercing 1,000,018' wrapping.
The overflow in that shot is amplified by the injected 1e6 hit: the reviewer's capture3 dealt 1e6 true damage. Estimated from the shot's chip widths (about 7.8 px per Mono character plus 12 px padding), realistic numbers overflow only when the labels total 37 or more characters, e.g. 'Physical 2,345 / Magic 1,234 / Piercing 456'. That is a late-game case, not every death.

CSS: src/ui/styles/hud.css:497 and :499.

polish.fix: Give .dchip `white-space: nowrap; flex: none` and .recap__types `flex-wrap: wrap`. Add a 'Held N s' line built from loss-of-control statuses in the same 15 s window.

polish.title: Feet glide flat on the floor in attack2, three casts and victory (no lift on the step-ins)

Give feet_from transitions a lift arc (6-8 cm, heel first, about 60 % of the move), plant by the impact frame, and pivot Swing Out on the lead toe with the trail foot in two lifted steps.

Better as one roster task: add the on-floor glide gate (no more than 2 cm of horizontal toe travel while within 1.5 cm of floor height) to every fighter's clipcheck, since Hesmi, Ervet, Burdam, Lisvel and Nurrow fail it too.
